directions.0: Short-horizon reversal and microstructure mean reversion under a dollar-neutral, cost-aware construction. Build the signal from residual (beta- and cross-sectional-market-adjusted) close-to-close and open-to-close returns over multiple short lookbacks (e.g. 1-10 sessions) combined by rank-averaging rather than fitting; explore volume-conditioned reversal (reversal stronger after high relative-volume, illiquid or gap-driven moves) and overnight-vs-intraday decomposition, since the execution lag is close-to-next-open. Key questions to answer empirically: (a) which horizon still survives the 5 bps per-side transaction cost at expected daily turnover, and what turnover budget (target annualized turnover band) maximizes net signal; (b) does the 30 bps annual borrow materially penalize the short leg, and should short-side eligibility be restricted by borrow cost proxy (use liquidity/volatility as proxy, no external data); (c) do reversal signals get crowded or flip sign after large market-wide shocks - condition on market return dispersion. Constraints you must respect in any code: max |weight| 0.02, gross <= 1.0, |net| <= 0.01 (so the book must be essentially dollar-neutral, long and short legs sized to match), each weight scaled to per-name risk so a single high-vol name cannot dominate variance. Deliver: one complete, deterministic generate_weights(history, universe) module with fixed a-priori parameters, NaN/eligibility handling (never trade ineligible or NaN-price names, zero them), no in-place mutation of history, and a short written report of train/validation diagnostics: gross/net, realized turnover, cost drag, per-name concentration, and stability of the signal sign across volatility regimes. If reversal fails on validation, say so explicitly and report the parameter region where it degrades rather than re-optimizing on validation.
directions.1: Cross-sectional and time-series momentum, with honest attention to the fact that the recent sample may contain a momentum crash regime. Build momentum from skip-a-recent-period cumulative returns at several lookbacks (e.g. 1-3, 6-12 months) plus a 52-week-high proximity variant and a simple moving-average trend filter, all rank-transformed so the signal is scale-free. Explore: (a) cross-sectional relative momentum vs time-series (own-history) momentum and their correlation; (b) volatility scaling of each name's signal (risk-adjusted momentum) and volatility targeting at the book level using a trailing realized-vol estimate of the strategy return, capped so the gross limit and 0.02 per-name cap are never violated; (c) regime conditioning using only price history (market trend, cross-sectional dispersion, trailing market realized vol, and drawdown state) to reduce exposure after crash-like states, with a small number of discrete buckets rather than fitted thresholds; (d) whether a short-leg-only or long-leg-only tilt is preferable given the 30 bps borrow cost and the net-tolerance constraint. Enforce dollar-neutrality (|net| <= 0.01), max |weight| 0.02, gross <= 1.0, and zero out ineligible/NaN names. No fitted predictive models: any threshold must be a stated prior (e.g. quantile of trailing history), not optimized on validation. Deliver a complete deterministic generate_weights module plus diagnostics on train vs validation: signal decay over holding periods, turnover, cost drag, hit rate of the top and bottom deciles, behavior in the worst 5% market weeks, and an explicit statement of which sub-signals you kept and why.
directions.2: Risk structure, low-volatility/beta-neutral anomaly and portfolio-level risk control. Investigate whether a low-beta, low-residual-volatility tilt earns a premium here and, more importantly, whether it gives a robust neutral book that survives the 0.02 cap and gross limit. Concretely: estimate betas and residual (idiosyncratic) volatility from trailing windows of daily returns versus an equal-weight or cap-free market proxy constructed from the universe itself (no external data); build long/short legs that are beta-neutral and residual-vol-matched so the portfolio's ex-ante volatility is minimized for a given gross; explore correlation-cluster grouping (simple clustering on trailing return correlation, or coarse beta/vol buckets as a substitute for sectors, which are unavailable) and cap exposure per cluster to avoid hidden concentration. Also test: (a) idiosyncratic-vol-scaled position sizing vs equal risk contribution; (b) drawdown-avoidance / crash filters using only own-price history (e.g. skip names in severe recent drawdowns or with extreme recent gap risk); (c) whether a jump/overnight-gap risk screen improves validation drawdown given that execution is at next open; (d) an ex-ante portfolio-volatility estimate and a rule that shrinks gross when estimated vol exceeds a stated prior threshold. Hard constraints: max |weight| 0.02, gross <= 1.0, |net| <= 0.01, deterministic, zero weights for ineligible/NaN names, no in-place mutation of history, efficient matrix math for ~500 names. Deliver a complete generate_weights module and a report comparing low-vol tilt vs pure risk-neutral construction: ex-ante and realized vol, max drawdown, cost drag, turnover, and how much of the return comes from the long leg vs short leg.
directions.3: Implementation, combination and validation discipline - you own the meta-layer, not a single alpha. Tasks: (1) Specify a combination protocol that rank-averages the dollar-neutral signal vectors produced by workers 0, 1 and 2 (or their sub-signals) with fixed, stated weights and a constraint-repair step: after averaging, cross-sectionally demean to force |net| <= 0.01, clip to max |weight| 0.02, then rescale to gross <= 1.0 without breaking neutrality; handle the case where clipping breaks neutrality by iterating the demean-clip-rescale loop a bounded number of times and documenting the residual. (2) Build a cost-aware turnover governor: given a per-side 5 bps cost and a target annualized turnover budget, blend the new target book with the prior book (or with a smoothed signal) using a partial-adjustment rule, and quantify the net-of-cost trade-off on train vs validation; also flag names whose expected edge is smaller than round-trip cost and set them to zero. (3) Audit eligibility and data hygiene: how to treat NaN history, newly listed names with short history, stale prices, and names that drop out of the universe (weights must still be returned for every universe ticker, zeros included); ensure no look-ahead (only data through the decision close) and no in-place mutation of the supplied history. (4) Design the validation protocol: propose a split (train/validation), the diagnostics each worker must report (gross, net, turnover, cost drag, annualized vol, max drawdown, decile spread, signal sign stability, concentration by vol/beta bucket), and a rule for accepting or rejecting a worker's signal that does not require re-fitting on validation - prefer rejecting a signal over tuning it. Deliver a complete deterministic generate_weights module implementing the combination and constraint-repair layer with placeholder sub-signal hooks, plus a concise written protocol that the other workers' modules must satisfy to be merged.

response.0: Research and code a constraint-aware cross-sectional short-horizon reversal strategy. Hypothesis: extreme 2-10 session returns and volume spikes, especially moves driven by liquidity or intraday overshoot, partially reverse in subsequent open-to-open returns. At decision close t use only history through t; separate overnight gaps from intraday returns; rank eligible stocks by residual reversal after controlling for recent momentum, realized volatility, dollar-volume/illiquidity, and price level. Build a dollar-neutral long-short book with roughly 20-50 names per side, absolute weight at most 0.02, gross at most 1.0, and absolute net exposure at most 0.01; return exactly one finite weight for every universe ticker including zeros. Use persistent signals, rank buffers, or coarse thresholds to limit turnover because transaction costs are 5 bps and short borrow is 30 bps annual. Test 1-, 3-, 5-, and 10-session horizons, winsorization, missing/eligibility handling, and whether skipping the most recent bar improves robustness. Return a hypothesis plus a complete deterministic generate_weights(history, universe) implementation.
response.1: Research and code a cross-sectional momentum and trend strategy with crash-risk controls. Hypothesis: 20-120 session relative strength and proximity to prior highs persist at the open-to-open horizon, while volatility normalization, residual momentum, and market/cross-sectional drawdown filters reduce momentum crashes. Use only adjusted price and volume history through the decision close. Explore lookbacks around 20, 60, and 120 sessions, intermediate skip periods, volatility scaling, 52-week-high proximity, volume confirmation, and regime filters based on trailing equal-weight market returns and cross-sectional dispersion. Build a dollar-neutral long-short portfolio with absolute weight at most 0.02, gross at most 1.0, absolute net exposure at most 0.01, and all universe tickers included with zeros. Compare pure momentum with residual momentum after neutralizing short-term reversal and low-volatility exposure. Manage turnover with coarse ranks or persistent thresholds rather than daily rank churn, and explicitly discuss whether the edge survives 5 bps transaction costs. Return a hypothesis plus complete generate_weights(history, universe) code.
response.2: Research and code a defensive low-risk and liquidity strategy without fundamentals. Hypothesis: stocks with low idiosyncratic volatility, stable dollar volume, shallow drawdowns, and high liquidity outperform or avoid crash losses relative to high-risk or illiquid peers, and a market-neutral low-risk factor can be robust after controlling for reversal and momentum. Use adjusted close/volume history to compute multi-window realized volatility, beta to an equal-weight market proxy, downside volatility, Amihud-style illiquidity, volume stability, drawdown, and correlation to the market. Build dollar-neutral portfolios such as long low-risk/short high-risk or long liquid/short illiquid with absolute weight at most 0.02, gross at most 1.0, absolute net exposure at most 0.01, and a finite weight for every universe name including zeros. Test whether the low-volatility tilt survives liquidity, reversal, and momentum controls, and whether a regime filter based on cross-sectional volatility helps. Emphasize robust constraint projection, eligibility filtering, NaN handling, and turnover control under 5 bps costs. Return a hypothesis plus complete generate_weights(history, universe) code.
response.3: Research and code a close-to-next-open microstructure strategy using intraday and overnight information. Hypothesis: today's open-close path, overnight gap, close location within the high-low range, range expansion, and abnormal volume predict next-session open-to-open returns, and may diversify classic reversal and momentum signals. Use only open, high, low, close, adjusted_open, adjusted_close, volume, and eligible fields through decision close t. Construct features such as overnight gap from prior close to today's open, intraday return from today's open to close, close location value, high-low range relative to volatility, volume surprise, and multi-day accumulations of these features. Build a dollar-neutral long-short book with absolute weight at most 0.02, gross at most 1.0, absolute net exposure at most 0.01, and all universe tickers returned with zeros. Test gap reversal versus continuation, conditioning on liquidity and broad market state, and turnover sensitivity because execution occurs at the next open. Include a critique of which signals are most likely to be spurious due to next-open execution and bid-ask effects. Return a hypothesis plus complete generate_weights(history, universe) code.
